text:
alex_support: FYI got an escalation from a customer (Acme QA) — their ingestion job hits our JSON-mode endpoint and we see repeated parse failures. They pasted logs, sending here.

alex_support: Customer log snippet:
```
RequestID: req_0a1b2c3d
POST /v1/generate { json_mode: true, stream: true }
Payload: 
{
  "orders": [
    {"temp_id": "t-123", "price": 12.5},
    {"id": "o-456", "price": 7.0}  // sometimes id present, sometimes missing
  ]
}
Error: Invalid JSON output from model: Unexpected token t in JSON at position 15
```

maria_sre: Can you confirm whether they use streaming or non-streaming? Streamed responses often get split mid-item and our client-side assembly can create `temp_*` artefacts.

alex_support: They set `stream: true` on the request (customer insists they need low-latency). They also said the model sometimes emits arrays with missing `id` keys and extra `temp_id` keys that our parser treats as spurious.

devin_ml: Can you paste the exact model name + parameters? Also which SDK version are they using? There are known cases where older SDKs rename fields when retrying.

alex_support: Model: open-instruct-2.5b (verified on our catalog). Params: {"json_mode": true, "stream": true, "max_tokens": 512}. SDK: python-sdk v0.9.1 (they're on older). RequestID above is the one mapped to their billing spike.

alex_support: Repro curl they shared:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-cust-xxx' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"json_mode":true,"stream":true,"prompt":"...","orders":[{"price":12.5},{"id":"o-456","price":7.0}]}'
```

alex_support: Failure seen server-side after streaming assembly: our JSON validator rejects final string because it contains a `temp_id` token outside quotes when an item was cut mid-stream: e.g. model output fragment -> `..., {temp_id: t-123, "price":12.5}, ...` which is invalid JSON.

devin_ml: Sounds like two issues colliding: (1) streaming boundary can split inside an object, leaving unquoted tokens; (2) customer payloads have optional `id` which leads their downstream schema to assume ordering by id. For immediate mitigation: ask customer to (A) disable stream and retry or (B) switch to `streaming_boundary":"item"` so we flush at item granularity (if their client supports it). Could also suggest upgrading SDK to v1.2+ which handles partial-item reassembly.

jon_prodops: Heads up: billing saw a spike tied to req_0a1b2c3d. Looks like retries increased token counts x2. We should check whether failed parses retried automatically client-side and doubled billed tokens.

alex_support: I told them to disable streaming and run a non-streamed request to confirm whether output is valid. Also asked them to upgrade SDK. I'm opening an internal escalation for runtime to consider a server-side guard that rejects unescaped bare tokens pre-parse and marks failure as non-billable when parse fails before finalization.

maria_sre: Can we add a quick server-side transform/perf-penalty flag to do a lightweight quote-sanitize pass before validation? If it's cheap we can turn it on per-customer while they patch.

devin_ml: For long-term, runtime should expose `json_mode_options`: {"strict_keys": ["id"], "stream_item_boundary": true, "sane_fallback": true}. Short-term regex that detects unquoted identifiers in output: `(?<!")\btemp_id\b(?!")` — we can flag and drop the response.

alex_support: Customer confirmed non-streamed call returns clean JSON. They'll patch to include `id` in every item. I'll escalate to runtime for a temporary safety net + patch the billing flag for req_0a1b2c3d to review double-charge.

raven_bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-1423 linked to req_0a1b2c3d — assigned to eng-runtime.

alex_support: Thanks — I'll follow up with the customer and paste back telemetry. :thumbsup:
